name: Self-hosted runners
summary: The vendor keeps the control plane (session queue, interface and transcripts) while sessions execute on runners your organization deploys inside its own network, the same idea as self-hosted CI runners. Runners poll the vendor over outbound HTTPS, claim queued sessions and run them next to internal services. Isolating sessions and restricting their egress is the operator's job.
how: Create an environment in the vendor's admin settings
Deploy runners on your hosts, for example on Kubernetes or Docker Compose
Runners poll the vendor's queue over outbound HTTPS and claim sessions
Each session clones the repository and runs on your host; model calls go to the vendor's API by default
facts: Claude Code cloud sessions (public beta on Team and Enterprise, off by default)
Outbound only; the vendor never connects into your network
Claude Code: api.anthropic.com by default, or Bedrock or Google Cloud
Checkouts and builds stay on your machines, but you run the fleet and its isolation
goodFor: Keeping checkouts and build artifacts on your infrastructure
watchOut: Runners execute model-directed code: isolate per session and default-deny egress
Prompts, responses and tool results still go to the vendor
You build the runner image and operate the fleet
